paragraphs: Tyne and Wear has no single council for children's services. Fostering here is run by five local services: Newcastle City Council, Gateshead Council, North Tyneside Council, South Tyneside Council and Together for Children, which runs children's services for Sunderland. The independent agencies shown above also approve carers across the area. Newcastle, Gateshead, North Tyneside and Sunderland each have their own page on this site, with more detail for that place.

All five belong to Foster with North East, a recruitment and support hub shared by 12 councils across the region and backed by the Department for Education. It acts as the first point of contact for anyone thinking about fostering, passes each enquiry to the right council and supports applicants through the process with information sessions, events and training. When it marked its first year in October 2024, the hub said it had received more than 850 enquiries and that applications were taking 4.8 months to reach approval, against a national average of six. South Tyneside says the councils are also working together on the Mockingbird programme from The Fostering Network.

Our Newcastle pay page shows what one Tyne and Wear council pays: a weekly allowance for each child from £182 to £267 by age, plus a fee per child that starts at £106.65 or £159.98 a week for mainstream care, depending on the child's age, and rises for children with more complex needs. The council's page does not give the year, so check the current figures with its fostering team.

Every fostering service in Tyne and Wear must pay at least the national minimum allowance for England outside London and the South East, which for 2026-27 is £176 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £182 for 3 to 4, £201 for 5 to 10, £227 for 11 to 15 and £267 for 16 to 17. Speak to your own council and to two or three of the agencies above, and compare support and training as well as pay.
